name: Selhorst Woodworks | Las Vegas/San Diego | Accent Walls and Ceilings, Barn Doors, Shelving, Beams
old_description: Selhorst Woodworks was built on a shared vision between husband-and-wife team Matthew and Chantel Selhorst: to create exceptional spaces through thoughtful design, expert craftsmanship, and an unwavering commitment to quality.
about:
Selhorst Woodworks operates from Las Vegas, Nevada, where husband-and-wife team Matthew and Chantel Selhorst founded the company on a shared vision to create exceptional spaces through thoughtful design and expert craftsmanship. The business identifies as family-owned and grew from a passion for woodworking into a custom finish carpentry operation serving the Las Vegas area.

The shop produces custom architectural woodwork including accent walls and ceilings, barn doors, shelving, built-ins, mudrooms, beams, baseboards, and crown molding. It also offers wallpaper installation and design services, and works with specialty materials such as Thermory thermally modified wood and Renson products. The company describes its approach as delivering meticulous attention to detail from consultation through final installation.

Clients include homeowners, interior designers, builders, and architects who value timeless design and craftsmanship. Projects range from residential upgrades to custom millwork for new construction, with the team emphasizing seamless integration of custom features into existing or new spaces.

The founders state that the company was built on an unwavering commitment to quality and the belief that the smallest details make the biggest impact. They position the business around a family-first philosophy, treating each project with the same care they would apply to their own home, and aim to create spaces that are both beautifully designed and built to be enjoyed for years.

name: Sentinel Solar
old_description: Sentinel Solar specializes in premium residential solar + storage systems designed for performance, resilience, and longevity. We handle everything from permitting to utility approval, and we build systems we'd put on our own homes.
about:
Sentinel Solar is based in Covington, Kentucky, and serves customers across Kentucky and Ohio. The company was founded by Jan Thurman, who brought over a decade of coast-to-coast experience in residential and commercial solar to establish a firm built on the conviction that solar should be done right or not at all.

The company designs and installs custom solar-plus-storage systems for homes and businesses, handling every step from permitting and utility approval to final commissioning. Its services include residential solar with battery backup, commercial solar arrays, EV charger installation, and generator integration. All work is performed by Sentinel's own crews rather than subcontractors, and recent projects include installations at a private residence in Fort Mitchell, Kentucky, and at Wenzel Distillery and ProMaster in Cincinnati, Ohio.

The company emphasizes long-term relationships over volume, positioning itself as a premium provider rather than a high-volume installer.

Thurman founded the business to offer a local, accountable alternative to national franchises. The company cites four guiding principles: a consultative, non-transactional sales approach; local accountability with a team that lives in the community; installer-first quality that prioritizes safe, correct installation; and a referral-driven model that depends on long-term customer satisfaction.

name: Servall Uniform & Linen Supply
old_description: A professional appearance is the groundwork for your reputation. It affects your staff every day, from attitude and team spirit to quality of work. At Servall Uniform & Linen Supply, we are dedicated to making sure your business looks its best while upholding comfort and safety at the same time. Because we’re not only serving you, we’re serving the community that relies on you. When clean cannot be compromised, count on your partners at Servall Uniform & Linen Supply for dependable linen rentals and uniform services.
about:
Servall Uniform & Linen Supply was founded in 1938 in Rapid City, South Dakota. From its start serving hometown businesses, the company has grown to operate across a two-state region, with physical locations in Chamberlain, South Dakota, and Gillette, Wyoming (and an office in Cheyenne, Wyoming).

The company provides uniform rental and direct purchase, linen rental, industrial laundry services, restroom and sanitation supplies, janitorial products, first aid kits, dust control mats, towel and bedding programs, hand sanitizer stations, and ice melt. Servall manages scheduled pickup and delivery for its rental programs, serving hundreds of customers throughout western South Dakota and eastern Wyoming from its regional facilities.

Customers include healthcare providers such as Spearfish Canyon Healthcare, hospitality landmarks like Wall Drug, publishing operations such as Ravellette Publications, financial institutions including First Interstate Bank, and independent retailers like Alternative Fuel Coffee House. The company’s service area covers communities from Spearfish, Custer, and Hot Springs in South Dakota to Sheridan, Gillette, and Buffalo in Wyoming.

Servall emphasizes reliable, locally based service and the convenience of consolidated facility supply programs. Its stated mission is to provide dedicated, professional service that delivers cost value and enhanced productivity within weeks, backed by long-tenured delivery representatives who build ongoing relationships with client sites.

name: Service Electric Cable TV & Communications - Bethlehem HQ
old_description: An affordable alternative to traditional cable television at only $19.95 per month with hundreds of live bonus channels and NO network fees, cable TV fees, sports channel fees or rental fees!  Bonus channels include more than 70 Spanish language channels, 40+ true crime options, music, news, weather, kids channels and much more!
about:
Service Electric Cable TV & Communications traces its roots to 1948 in Mahanoy City, Pennsylvania, where John Walson Sr. (born John Walsonavich) invented cable television to bring broadcast signals to his appliance-store customers in the mountains. The company moved its headquarters to 2200 Avenue A in Bethlehem in 2014 and remains a third-generation, family-owned business now led by John M. Walson, grandson of the founder.

The company operates as a regional telecommunications provider delivering broadband internet (up to Gig+ speeds with eero whole-home WiFi), cable television with hundreds of channels including local sports networks such as the Service Electric Network (SEN) and SEN+ streaming app, and voice services. It also runs a dedicated business division — Service Electric Business — supplying internet, phone, and TV to small, medium, and enterprise customers with a promise of free local, same-day service calls. Service territory spans the Lehigh Valley, Hunterdon County (NJ), and Wilkes-Barre (PA).

Customers include residential subscribers and businesses across northeastern Pennsylvania and western New Jersey. Partnerships with PenTeleData and Alianza extend the portfolio to hosted voice and advanced broadband solutions.

The Walson family emphasizes community involvement and local ownership as differentiators: the company was the first in the nation to carry HBO (1972), a founding partner of the Lehigh Valley IronPigs and Phantoms, and operates the hyper-local Service Electric Network covering high school and collegiate sports, Musikfest, and regional news.

name: Service Metal Fabricators
old_description: Service Metal Fabricators is a one-stop shop providing comprehensive precision sheet metal fabrication services for over 40 years. As a full-service fabricator specializing in NEMA and other electronic enclosures, brackets, panels and assemblies, along with stainless steel medical containers, our services have proven integral to a wide range of customers in various industries. Our enclosures often house the printed circuit boards and other internal electronic data processing, controlling and actuating parts for products serving unique purposes in the electronics, industrials, diagnostic/measurement and various other industries.
about:
Service Metal Fabricators, based in Williamsburg, Virginia, has operated for over 40 years as a precision sheet metal fabricator.

The shop produces NEMA-rated enclosures, brackets, panels, assemblies, and stainless-steel medical containers. Its capabilities span shearing, CNC punching, press brake forming, vertical milling, CNC machining, MIG/TIG and spot welding, riveting, hardware insertion, silk screening, chemical finishing, powder coating, and painting. Operations run from a 12-acre campus with 56,000 to 60,000 square feet of manufacturing space, supported by a production workforce that includes three quality-assurance professionals for every 25 production employees.

Customers come from electronics, industrial equipment, diagnostic and measurement, medical, aerospace, military, TEMPEST computing, solar energy, and transportation sectors. Notable programs include enclosures for Becton Dickinson’s laboratory blood analyzers, chassis for a $15 billion transportation company’s electronics division, components for a solar smart-circuitry venture, and helm stations installed on the bridges of a dozen U.S. aircraft carriers.

The company differentiates itself through vertical integration that includes its own delivery fleet, offering free shipping within 200 miles, and machine redundancy to protect lead times. It also provides design engineering, design-for-manufacturability guidance, and reverse-engineering support, while maintaining adherence to military and industry standards such as AMS-STD-1595, MIL-DTL-5541, and RoHS.

Smoker’s long‑standing passion for fine millwork led him to start the company, which has since grown into a team of skilled craftsmen dedicated to turning raw wood into finished architectural pieces.

The shop produces architectural millwork, custom cabinetry, custom doors, commercial millwork, private‑label and white‑label furniture, and metalwork. Operations run from a facility on King Court, where the team handles projects ranging from residential cabinetry to large‑scale commercial installations for restaurants and hotels.

Seven Trees emphasizes a willingness to take on challenging projects that other shops decline, positioning itself as a problem‑solver for complex millwork and furniture requirements.

name: Severance Foods / Pan De Oro
old_description: Pan De Oro is a family owned and operated brand that has been producing delicious tortilla chips for almost 40 years.  Our attention to high-quality standards, all natural ingredients and unique flavors all play a key part in why our chips are so delicious!
about:
Severance Foods operates from Hartford, Connecticut, where it was founded in 1985 by three former Heublein food scientists — Richard Stevens, John Grikis, and Rich Dana. After R.J. Reynolds acquired Heublein in 1984, the trio used their severance packages to acquire a facility and equipment, launching a company to meet the Northeast's growing demand for tortillas and tortilla chips. The business remains family-owned and operated under the Pan De Oro brand.

The company manufactures tortilla chips and salsa under its own Pan De Oro label and provides co-packing services for other brands. Production emphasizes non-GMO, organic, and hand-crafted methods. The plant in Hartford is described as the largest tortilla chip manufacturer and co-packer in the Northeast, though specific facility size, headcount, and volume figures are not disclosed.

Customers include restaurants, schools, concession operators, and retail grocery stores across New York, New Jersey, and Pennsylvania, as well as farmers markets throughout the region. The co-packing side serves other food brands seeking a regional production partner.

The founders started the business after their work on Ortega Mexican Foods at Heublein revealed an unmet need for Mexican-style products in the Northeast. They cite attention to high-quality standards, all-natural ingredients, and unique flavor development as the reasons their chips have gained traction since 1985.

about:
Sheet Metal Enterprises operates from Dedham, Massachusetts, on the Boston-Dedham line near I-95. The company has been in business for more than a decade, positioned minutes from local HVAC supply houses.

The shop specializes in custom-fabricated HVAC ductwork and fittings, producing ducts in standard 4-foot and 8-foot lengths as well as precise custom sizes such as 74 3/4 inches. Beyond ductwork, it manufactures copper shower pans and other sheet metal products, including soldering brass strainers into the pans. The operation emphasizes quick turnaround for a custom fabrication facility.

The company's proximity to supply houses and its job-site delivery service support contractors who need accurately sized ductwork on tight schedules.

Ed's field background informs the company's approach: he guides customers on sizing and duct design, offering practical installation insights. The business was built to make the procurement and installation process smoother, combining custom fabrication with direct delivery to the job site.

name: SiCamore Semi
old_description: More efficient drivetrains using semiconductor technologies based on Wide Band Gap (WBG) materials such as Silicon Carbide (SiC) are enabling engineers to achieve high voltage (1.2 – 3.3KV) and high power demands in a cost-effective way.
about:
SiCamore Semi operates a pure-play semiconductor foundry in Bend, Oregon. The company describes itself as a U.S.-based boutique foundry with three decades of experience in wafer fabrication, though a specific founding year is not disclosed.

The foundry specializes in high-power, high-voltage wide-bandgap devices using silicon carbide (SiC) and gallium nitride (GaN) on 100 mm and 150 mm wafers. Its process flow covers photolithography with ASML 5000 I-line steppers and Karl Suss aligners, thin-film deposition (sputtering, PVD, CVD, PECVD, e-beam evaporation), frontside and backside metallization, thermal oxidation and diffusion, wet and dry etching (RIE), rapid thermal annealing, and ion implantation (cold and hot). SiC-specific steps include high-temperature implant and anneal, gate oxidation with nitric oxide anneal, and a dedicated gold wafer fab for high-reliability, radiation-hardened, and RF devices. Additional partner services encompass device design, wafer thinning, dicing, packaging, and test.

SiCamore serves electric-vehicle, medical, industrial, aerospace and defense, and academic customers. It supplies SiC diodes, MOSFETs, JBSFETs, JFETs, IGBTs, and Si SGTOs/SDIODEs for industrial power and switching applications. The company also collaborates with universities on NASA, NSF, DOE, and DOD grants focused on space, grid, weapons, EV, data-center, and communications technologies, and it targets U.S. military, intelligence, and government agencies alongside commercial transportation, telecommunications, and healthcare infrastructure markets.

The company states its mission is to deliver innovative power-semiconductor solutions through the development of silicon and wide-bandgap technologies. It aims to become the power-semiconductor facility in the U.S. Northwest for advanced wide-bandgap device fabrication, integration, and testing, emphasizing a stable, ITAR-certified environment for aerospace and defense programs.

old_description: At Sierra Metals Southwest LLC, we specialize in crafting exceptional architectural and ornamental metals in the Las Vegas area. With a passion for precision and design, we offer both standard and custom solutions to elevate commercial, residential, or artistic spaces. From intricate details to bold elements our expert team delivers high quality metal work tailored to your vision.
about:
Sierra Metals Southwest LLC operates from a facility in Las Vegas, Nevada. The company does not publish a founding date, but its ownership group brings more than 40 years of metal‑fabrication experience to the business. Sierra Metals is part of a family of companies that includes Andy Russo Jr Inc, a union installation specialist, and Magnus Ornamental Metals, which focuses on ornamental and residential metalwork.

The shop provides architectural and ornamental metal fabrication using a range of processes: MIG welding of steel, TIG welding of stainless steel, brass and aluminum; shearing up to 3/16‑inch mild steel in 12‑foot lengths; ACM routing; polishing to #4, #6 and #8 finishes; light‑gauge bending up to 16 gauge in 12‑foot lengths; CAD design support; water‑jet cutting; and plasma cutting. From these capabilities it produces both standard and custom items such as fences, gates, decorative handrails and ceilings, door frames and guards, shade panels, louvers, trellises, security screens, art sculptures, ACM panels, metal soffit, fascia, trim, wall panels and standing‑seam roofing panels.

Sierra Metals serves commercial, residential and artistic clients in the Las Vegas region. A noted collaboration is with F&A Modular Homes, for which Sierra Metals designs and fabricates metal components for modular housing units. The sister firms extend the offering to union‑grade installation and residential ornamental work.

The company states that its differentiation rests on four values: craftsmanship that blends skill with artistry, innovation that pushes custom solutions, customer focus that builds lasting relationships, and reliability that honors promises with timely service.

about:
Sigla Furniture operates from a workshop and warehouse in Los Angeles, California. The business traces its roots to 1976 when the founder arrived from Iran; by the early 1980s he had opened a small woodworking shop after initially importing Italian music boxes. Now a second-generation, family-owned company, it has served the Los Angeles area for over four decades.

The company handcrafts traditional and transitional furniture — dining tables, sofas, chairs, case goods and accessories — each built to order in its Los Angeles facility using premium imported materials. Production relies on artisan joinery such as dovetail joints, custom wood finishing, and tailored upholstery in fabric, leather or velvet. Orders are made to specification from a sketch or SKU, with a typical lead time of eight to ten weeks.

Sigla serves residential clients, interior designers, and the hospitality sector. Commercial references include the Omni Hotel, the Shade Hotel and the Marriott. The 2022 acquisition of JDM Furniture and Unfinished Chairs added raw frame offerings and expanded capacity for large-scale projects.

The firm emphasizes heirloom-quality craftsmanship backed by a one-year repair guarantee (the Sigla Guarantee). Its family legacy and made-in-USA approach are positioned as the reason customers return for pieces intended to last generations.

about:
Siri Wire Co. has operated from Danielson, Connecticut since its founding in 1992. The company is a fourth‑generation family business with more than 50 years of industry experience, and it remains led by the family that built it from the ground up.

The company manufactures and stocks stainless steel and alloy wire, serving customers across North America. Its product range includes electro‑polish quality (EPQ) wire — held in one of the largest domestic stocking positions in the region — as well as cold‑heading and spring wire grades such as 302, 304, 316, 17‑7, 302HQ, 303, 316L, 410, 416, 420, and 430. Siri Wire also provides annealing via strand annealing furnaces, coating and redraw services for customer‑supplied material, and straight‑and‑cut processing. Through its affiliation with Tri Star Metals and the Bender Wire Group, the company now operates behind two fully operational American production mills, enabling domestic melt, DFARS‑compliant, and non‑DFARS material options.

Siri Wire serves medical and surgical device manufacturers, aerospace and defense contractors, automotive suppliers, fastener and cold‑heading producers, filter screen and washer makers, and general industrial customers. Common applications include springs, fasteners, medical equipment, filter screens, washers, and rings.

The company emphasizes its ISO 9001 certification, American‑made production, and a team that stands behind every order. Differentiators cited by the company include same‑day and short lead‑time shipping on stocked EPQ wire, the backing of two domestic mills for broader product range and engineering support, and a family‑owned culture focused on integrity and competitive pricing.

Beavers started the company to escape the industry’s “careless ways” — mismanaged production, poor communication, and unmet deadlines. The firm emphasizes open, fair, team‑focused service and holds WBE certification, a CAGE code (8RA44), and SAM.gov registration for government work.

about:
Spotted Owl Timber, Inc. operates a sawmill in Santa Fe, New Mexico. The company was founded in 1991 by David Lindsey, a third-generation sawmill operator born and raised in New Mexico’s logging industry. Lindsey launched the business with a small Woodmizer band mill to supply beams and lumber for the growing demand for southwestern-style homes in Santa Fe and northern New Mexico.

The sawmill produces natural, custom wood products from locally sourced softwood species — Ponderosa pine, white fir, Douglas fir, and Engelmann spruce. Using a larger Woodmizer thin-kerf band mill and additional equipment, the operation cuts beams, dimensional lumber, and custom profiles. The thin-kerf blade reduces waste and yields up to 30 percent more lumber per log compared with traditional circle saws. All material is harvested by independent local loggers and processed without added chemicals.

Customers include contractors, private homebuilders, and the general public throughout northern New Mexico. The company’s products are used primarily in residential construction and custom home projects that emphasize regional architectural styles.

Lindsey started Spotted Owl to meet a specific regional need for locally milled, natural wood suited to southwestern designs. The company highlights its sustainable sourcing, thin-kerf efficiency, and chemical-free processing as key differentiators.

Its customers include meat and poultry plants, prepared‑foods facilities, and packaging operations that rely on equipment from the OEMs listed above. Stone Enterprises positions itself as a cost‑saving alternative to original‑equipment manufacturers, offering parts that meet or exceed OEM specifications.

Stone Enterprises emphasizes an “under promise and over deliver” philosophy and backs every replacement part with a 100% satisfaction guarantee. old_description: SunGold Foods Inc., a division of Red River Commodities, creates roasted ingredients and food products to meet your specific formulations and specifications. We also provide custom packaging solutions to fit your needs and desires.
about:
SunGold Foods Inc., a division of Red River Commodities, operates from Fargo, North Dakota. The company specializes in producing roasted ingredients and food products tailored to customer formulations and specifications, along with custom packaging solutions.

The facility roasts products using both oil frying and dry roasting methods. For frying, it employs NuSun sunflower oil, a trans-fat-free oil with minimal flavor transfer. Dry roasting is performed in multiple configurations to achieve distinct flavor profiles. The company's roasting lines are designed for continuous flow, reducing variation in finished goods. Master Roasters oversee each batch to meet taste, texture, and visual requirements. SunGold also develops custom flavors and proprietary pre-blends in collaboration with clients, and maintains a completely peanut- and tree nut-free environment.

SunGold serves food manufacturers and brands that require custom-roasted ingredients, particularly those needing nut-free and allergen-controlled products. Its quality system monitors every step from seed selection and planting through harvest, storage, processing, packaging, and delivery. On-site testing includes moisture, color, salt levels, residual oxygen, bag weights, coding, seal integrity, and package appearance. Nitrogen flushing is used to remove oxygen from packages and prevent oxidation.

The company holds AIB, Kosher, Organic, and SQF Food Safety certifications, reflecting its focus on human food standards, high purity, and identity preservation. These certifications, combined with its science-based roasting approach and dedicated Master Roasters, form the basis of its differentiation in the custom roasting and packaging market.

about:
Taiyo America Inc. operates from Carson City, Nevada, where it was established in 1990 as the manufacturing subsidiary of Japan's Taiyo Holdings Co., Ltd. (founded 1953). The company began as a supplier of solder mask products and has since expanded its portfolio to serve the printed circuit board industry across North America and Europe.

The company produces a range of electronic materials including the PSR-4000 family of liquid photoimageable solder masks, legend inks, thermal management inks, direct imaging products, hole-plugging and gap-filling compounds, and dielectric and conductive inks for printed electronics. It also designs and manufactures PCB coating and drying equipment under the Taiyo Circuit Automation brand. Processes supported include screen printing, spray coating, curtain coating, inkjet deposition, and UV LED curing (360–420 nm).

Taiyo America serves aerospace and defense, medical, automotive, and consumer electronics sectors. Its materials have been qualified for programs such as the F-35 fighter jet, the Mars MER-1 rover, the X-59 Quesst X-plane, and satellite platforms. In medical devices, they are used in hearing aids, blood pressure monitors, imaging equipment, and robotic systems. Automotive applications include electric vehicles, brake systems, vacuum pumps, and LED lighting. Consumer electronics encompass smartphones, smartwatches, laptops, tablets, and desktop computers.

The company emphasizes three differentiators: a proven track record as the global market leader in specialty inks and solder masks; service delivered by regional sales, engineering, and support teams across North America and Europe; and innovations driven by heavy R&D investment, exemplified by the high-resolution FLEXFINER dry film, inkjet solder masks, and next-generation thermal management products. Taiyo also notes that in-stock items typically ship by the end of the next business day.

about:
Tasly Pharmaceuticals, Inc. was founded in 2006 and is headquartered in Rockville, Maryland. The company was established to integrate botanical science with modern pharmaceutical innovation, developing safe and effective botanical medicines that complement conventional treatments.

The company’s core focus is the development and manufacture of botanical drugs, most notably T89 (Dantonic®), a herbal medicine-derived compound that has completed an FDA Phase III global clinical trial. Manufacturing takes place on what the company describes as the world’s largest proprietary automatic dripping pill and packaging production line, a fully automated system featuring digital control, high-speed operation, precision pill counting, real-time imprint monitoring, and automated defect removal. The production process follows Good Extracting Practice (GEP) covering extraction, condensation, chromatography, crystallization, filtration, and drying, while quality systems adhere to Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP), Good Agricultural Practice (GAP), and Good Laboratory Practice (GLP). Tasly reports more than 500 worldwide regulatory approvals for its products.

The company has presented Phase III clinical data for T89 at the American College of Cardiology (ACC) 2018, participated in the Trade Winds ASEAN Mission and Business Forum in 2023, and exhibited at BioJapan in 2022, indicating engagement with global pharmaceutical markets and research communities.

Tasly’s stated differentiation rests on bridging traditional healing wisdom with rigorous clinical validation, aiming to revolutionize patient care through scientifically validated botanical medicines. The company emphasizes its first-in-class FDA Phase III achievement for a botanical drug and its fully automated, digitally controlled production line as key factors that set it apart.

TechNH, Inc. was founded in 1982 in a small corner of a Nashua, New Hampshire mill building. Now headquartered in Merrimack, NH, the company has grown from a modest operation into a global precision injection molder.

Testimonials reference clients in Massachusetts, Pennsylvania, and New Hampshire, including healthcare and industrial OEMs. The company assigns each project a dedicated team comprising an account manager, customer service representative, program manager, and a degreed plastics engineer.

TechNH emphasizes a 5-step tool transfer process designed to protect supply continuity and confirm tool condition without production downtime. Core values—adaptability, integrity, enthusiasm, pride in work, and reliability—guide operations. Nearly 40% of the workforce has more than five years' tenure, and about a quarter have exceeded a decade, reflecting a culture the company cites as a differentiator.

about:
Texas Instruments traces its roots to 1930 when Geophysical Service Inc., an oil and gas exploration venture, opened in Dallas, Texas. The founders’ entrepreneurial drive led the company into electronics during World War II, and by 1951 it was renamed Texas Instruments Incorporated.

TI designs, fabricates, packages, and tests analog and embedded processing chips, offering a portfolio of more than 80,000 products. Its global manufacturing network includes 300 mm wafer fabs that run on 100 % renewable electricity, and the company reports producing tens of billions of chips each year. With roughly 33,000 employees and over 100,000 customers, TI handles everything from process technology and design through final test and delivery.

The company’s components serve automotive, industrial, consumer electronics, communications, data center, personal electronics, and medical equipment markets. Engineers at automakers, industrial automation firms, smartphone makers, and data‑center operators rely on TI’s analog ICs, microcontrollers, and wireless transceivers for applications ranging from vehicle electrification to AI‑driven servers.

TI says its founding purpose was to make electronics more affordable through semiconductors, a mission that still guides its three core ambitions: act like long‑term owners, adapt to a changing world, and build a company its people are proud of. The firm emphasizes supply‑chain resilience, noting that its manufacturing expertise lets customers get products when they need them, regardless of geopolitical conditions.

old_description: Offering custom compounding to meet customer’s needs since 1973
about:
The Plastics Group of America (TPG) is headquartered in Woonsocket, Rhode Island, where it was founded in 1973 by Bob Lebeaux as Ralco Industries, a one-man scrap trading operation. The business adopted its current name in 1988 after merging Ralco, the Polifil® compounding line, and the Transcontinental Polymers recycling unit.

TPG operates over 300,000 square feet of manufacturing space in Woonsocket and runs a 24/7 production schedule. Its core business is custom compounding of Polifil® polypropylene-based reinforced resins, using mineral, talc, calcium, glass, and barium additives to meet specific physical, mechanical, and thermal requirements. An on-site quality control laboratory equipped with melt index, Izod, flexural, tensile, DSC, moisture, ash, Gardner impact, and color testing instruments certifies every batch, whether the order is 100 pounds or one million pounds. The company also provides recycling and toll processing services, densifying, guillotining, and extruding scrap into reusable material, and acts as a resin broker and distributor with stocking points across the continental United States.

The compounded resins serve processors in appliance, automotive, construction, consumer housewares and disposables, furniture, industrial/institutional/electronic, medical and personal care, packaging, and pump/pool/spa/irrigation markets. TPG's ISO 9001-certified facility supplies molders, extruders, and blow-molding operations that require consistent, specification-grade thermoplastics.

TPG emphasizes its asset-based manufacturing model combined with a full-service approach: free commercial color matching, technical consulting through its TPGOA Technical Insights library, and a commitment to on-time, on-budget delivery. The company traces its differentiation to the 1980 launch of custom compounding under the Polifil® brand and its early adoption of ISO 9002 certification in 1996, followed by an OSHA SHARP award in 1997.

name: The Wooden Nickel - Custom Live Edge Furniture
old_description: Every once in a while a project comes through the shop that reminds us why we started building furniture in the first place. This past spring, a family from Marshall County asked for a live edge dining table big enough to hold three generations at once. They...
about:
Based in Arab, Alabama, The Wooden Nickel builds custom live edge furniture from locally sourced hardwood slabs. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed; it operates as a shop where each piece begins with a slab selected for its natural character.

The shop produces dining tables, desks, adjustable workstations, and contract-grade furniture for commercial spaces. The process is deliberately slow: logs from tree services and loggers are kiln-dried and stabilized, then flattened, sanded, and inspected for cracks or knots that may receive resin filling. Finishes are applied in multiple hand-rubbed coats, and steel bases—fabricated from high-tolerance steel—are fitted to ensure level, wobble-free assembly. The company notes that most production is custom, ranging from single items to larger commercial orders.

Customers include residential clients such as a Marshall County family that commissioned a three-generation dining table, as well as local businesses needing tables and work surfaces for offices, break rooms, and public areas. The firm has supplied several area companies with thicker slabs, reinforced bases, and durable finishes designed for daily wear.

The Wooden Nickel emphasizes careful material selection, honest construction, and an unhurried timeline. As the owners describe it, the goal is furniture that 'doesn't draw attention to itself' but 'just keeps working year after year'—built to be used, built to last, and built for real life.

old_description: We design, engineer, and construct rugged steel front bumpers and rear bumpers for Chevy Silverado, Dodge RAM, Ford F-Series, and GMC Sierra trucks. We also make steel Jeep frames and skid plates. Everything we make is made from CNC laser cut PNO solid steel pate, and hand welded by certified professionals in Moore, Montana, USA. Each truck bumper we offer is better than the factory bumper, and comes with a lifetime warranty.
about:
Throttle Down Kustoms operates from Moore, Montana, where it was established in April 2004 after founder Jeremy Pulse purchased his former employer, Advance Frame Works. Pulse had begun building custom truck bumpers in his spare time during the early 2000s, and growing demand led him to transition to full-time fabrication.

The company designs, engineers, and builds steel front and rear bumpers for Chevrolet Silverado, Dodge Ram, Ford F-Series, and GMC Sierra trucks, as well as steel Jeep frames and skid plates. Production relies on CNC laser-cut PNO steel plate (3/16″ and 1/4″) and CNC mandrel-bent frames using 2″×4″ A500 rectangular tubing, all hand-welded by certified fabricators. A separate line, TreeDogKustoms, produces lightweight aluminum dog boxes for trucks, ATVs, and UTVs. The shop runs a dedicated team of certified fabricators, each trained in chassis fabrication programs.

Customers range from ranch hands and oil-field workers needing heavy-duty bumper upgrades to off-road enthusiasts seeking grille guards, integrated LED lighting, and rock-crawling frames. The company also fulfills custom fabrication requests such as enclosed trailers, street rods, and diesel-powered truggies. Products ship worldwide with a typical lead time of 8 to 12 weeks.

Throttle Down Kustoms emphasizes U.S. manufacturing, a lifetime warranty on every product, and mandrel-bent frames that avoid welded joints for greater strength and precision. Pulse’s WyoTech degree in Auto Body Technology and Chassis Fabrication underpins the engineering approach, and the company hires only graduates of reputable fabrication programs.

Thunderbird Molding operates from Elkhart, Indiana, with additional facilities in Shelbyville, Illinois, and Greensboro. The company is Thunderbird-owned and actively managed, though its founding year and founders are not publicly disclosed. It began as a resource for high-precision custom plastic injection molding and contract manufacturing.

The company provides comprehensive mold design, prototyping, engineering, production, and assembly services. Its capabilities include custom plastic injection molding, insert molding, over molding via press-to-press transfer, finishing, and secondary operations. With presses ranging up to 1,500 tons and an inventory of more than 800 molds, Thunderbird supports scalable production of parts in the millions as well as economical short-run projects using quick-mold-change systems and proprietary batch molding procedures. It also offers 3D printing for low-volume production using carbon printing technology.

Thunderbird serves medical device manufacturers, defense contractors, automotive OEMs, and producers of drinkware and lighting. The company has helped a medical device manufacturer achieve regulatory compliance and an automaker find solutions with advanced molding processes. Its lens-grade parts, made from contaminant-free polymers, meet critical defense industry specifications.

Thunderbird differentiates itself through repeatable part tolerances of ±0.0002 inches, automated 3D video inspection, and a quality system registered to ISO 9001:2015, ITAR, PPAP, SPI, and UL QMMY2. The company cites a 99% success rate when reworking close-tolerance molds to compensate for shrinkage and warpage, and a 2.5-second cycle time on an 8-cavity mold.

The woman-owned small business was incorporated in Minnesota by founder Mike DeLadi, who established the company on a principle of "No slogans, just service."

old_description: At Toray, we carefully design thoughtful materials that surround you; materials that help keep food fresh, provide protection against the sun’s rays, make cars more luxurious to the touch, add value to industrial applications, and much more.
about:
Toray Plastics (America), Inc. operates its headquarters in North Kingstown, Rhode Island, where its Torayfan® and Lumirror® film divisions are based. A second facility in Front Royal, Virginia houses the PEF foam division. The company is a wholly owned subsidiary of Toray Industries, Inc., a Japanese multinational founded in 1926 with over 47,900 employees across 308 subsidiaries worldwide. No founding date for the U.S. entity is disclosed, and the original founders are not named in public materials.

The company manufactures specialty polymer films and foams for converters and manufacturers that produce finished consumer and industrial goods. The Torayfan® division extrudes polypropylene and cast polypropylene films, including metallized OPP and bio-based PET variants. The Lumirror® division produces polyester (PET) films, also offered in metallized and bio-based grades. The PEF division extrudes polyolefin, polypropylene, and polyethylene foams. Together the divisions run multiple extrusion, metallizing, and coating lines, including proprietary LumiLid® extrusion coating systems (XXL5 and TXL5). Facility sizes and annual volumes are not published.

Toray's films and foams serve packaging, label, solar-control window, technical, housing and engineering, and automotive markets. Converters use the materials for food packaging that extends shelf life, for pressure-sensitive labels, for automotive window tinting, and for solar-control glazing in buildings and vehicles. The company cites automotive window tinting and food packaging as specific application examples.

Toray states its corporate philosophy is to contribute to society through the creation of new value with innovative ideas, technologies, and products. The U.S. operation emphasizes environmental sustainability, holding certifications such as ISO 14001, ISCC PLUS, and Rhode Island Green Manufacturing Certification, and frames its manufacturing approach as responsible stewardship for future generations.

Its capabilities span machining, drilling, milling, CNC turning (3- and 4-axis), sand blasting, powder coating, brazing, and part assembly. The shop handles everything from R&D prototypes and low-volume runs to full-scale production, delivering high-tolerance, mission-critical components.

Tri-Angle serves aerospace, defense, ordnance, electronics, and commercial industries. Customers rely on the company for aerospace-grade welds, multi-axis machined parts, and complex fabrications that meet strict compliance and performance requirements.

The company emphasizes quality assurance through AS/ISO-certified systems, in-process inspections, and NADCAP welding standards. It differentiates itself through collaborative partnerships, continual improvement via lean manufacturing and advanced process control, and a commitment to delivering parts right the first time — on spec, on budget, and on schedule.

name: Troy Brook Visions Fine Art Furniture Gallery and Studio
old_description: Tucked among the rolling hills of beautiful Litchfield, Connecticut is the studio and gallery of Troy Brook Visions, Inc., Makers of Fine Furniture. Master Artisan Daniel Gugnoni designs and creates exquisite custom handcrafted fine art furniture.
about:
The company was founded in 1993 by Daniel Gugnoni, a sculptor who turned to furniture making after earning a BFA. He established the business on the Shaker principles of hard work, honesty, and pride in craftsmanship. Barbara Mojon Gugnoni, who holds a BA in English literature and a background in advertising, joined the operation in 1996 and now handles marketing, sales, and the finishing process.

The studio produces one-of-a-kind and custom fine art furniture, each piece designed and built by Daniel Gugnoni. The workflow moves from client consultation through design, handcrafted joinery, and a proprietary twelve-step hand-rubbed finish applied by Barbara. The shop does not run production lines; every item is a unique functional sculpture. The facility is a small country barn studio and a second-floor gallery where finished pieces are displayed.

Troy Brook Visions has exhibited at juried events such as the American Craft Council Shows, the Paradise City Arts Festival, the Philadelphia Invitational Furniture Show, and the Fine Furnishings Show. These venues connect the studio with buyers who value handcrafted, design-driven furniture for residential settings.

The founders say the business exists to honor the material and the maker. Daniel Gugnoni describes each board as a gift from nature that should not be squandered, and the couple emphasizes that they never manufacture product—they create art. The Shaker-inspired ethos and the direct, personal involvement of both artisans in every commission are presented as the core differentiators.

old_description: Founded in April of 2002 by Curvin & Lucille Horning, Turntech started in a 2-car garage with one hydraulic copy lathe and a dream. Not to mention a mini fridge stocked with Mountain Dew and peanut butter cups!
about:
Turntech is based in Ephrata, Pennsylvania, and was founded in April 2002 by Curvin and Lucille Horning. The company began in a two-car garage with a single hydraulic copy lathe and a modest vision for custom wood turning.

Today, Turntech produces a wide range of custom wood products including columns, porch posts, mouldings, kitchen island legs, wooden balls, and dowels. The shop operates multiple CNC machines, highlighted by a custom CNC lathe capable of turning pieces up to 17½ inches in diameter and 144 inches long. Processes include reeding, rope twisting, barley twisting, and fluting, applied to wood species such as walnut, cherry, mahogany, maple, oak, cedar, pine, and poplar. The facility has expanded from its garage origins to a dedicated location in Lancaster County, though headcount and annual volume are not disclosed.

The company serves contractors restoring historic properties, homeowners updating staircases and entryways, furniture makers, stairway manufacturers, arts-and-crafts enthusiasts, and even martial-arts practitioners who use Turntech's wooden balls for training. Customers can submit photos, sketches, or CAD drawings for exact replication of existing designs.

Turntech emphasizes domestic production, made-to-order flexibility, and a typical turnaround of as little as five business days. The founders' original commitment to combining old-world craftsmanship with modern technology remains central, and the business stresses employment of local craftsmen and community involvement in Lancaster County.

about:
USA Injection Molding, a division of LMT Mercer Group, Inc., is headquartered in Lawrenceville, New Jersey. The parent company was formed in 1987 to supply the fence and deck industry with high-quality component parts.

The company operates as a full-service custom plastic injection molding facility with manufacturing plants in New Jersey and Ohio, plus distribution centers in New Jersey, Ohio, and Nevada. It runs 36 injection molding machines ranging from 60 to 1,000 tons, equipped with servo-robotics and nitrogen gas-assist capabilities. In-house tooling builds close to 100 new molds per year, from single-cavity prototypes to 64-cavity high-production molds. The facility stocks over 50 certified resins and operates a material testing laboratory. USA Injection Molding produces more than 950 fence, deck, and railing accessories and introduces at least 20 new products annually.

The company serves a broad range of industries including medical, military and defense, personal care, building and construction, housewares and consumer products, cosmetics, agricultural and farming, vinyl fence and railing, appliances, automotive, commercial food packaging, electronics, office products, and wood composite decking and railing. It also supports any industry requiring plastic injection molded components.

USA Injection Molding emphasizes domestic manufacturing, in-house engineering and tooling, rapid prototyping printed in hours, and distribution from three U.S. warehouses. Its stated mission is to be the industry leader in design, manufacturing, and distribution of plastic injection molding products by setting benchmarks for quality, customer service, and competitive pricing.

United & Turtle Mountain Communications is headquartered in Langdon, North Dakota, with additional offices in Bottineau and Rolla. The company traces its roots to February 1952, when it was established as the United Telephone Cooperative to bring telephone service to rural communities in northeastern North Dakota.

Customers range from individual households and small businesses to K‑12 school districts, governmental bodies, and other telecommunications providers that purchase wholesale transport and special circuits.

United describes its mission as keeping rural North Dakota communities strong by delivering essential communication services that allow people to connect, work, and thrive. As a designated Smart Rural Community provider, it emphasizes local decision‑making, community reinvestment through its educational foundation, and a workforce drawn from the towns it serves.

about:
Universal Enterprises Inc. was founded in 1992 in Shinnston, West Virginia, and operates as a small business enterprise. The company has served North American and international clients from its single-site facility for over three decades.

The 62,000-square-foot plant houses 50,000 square feet of shop space, 10,000 square feet of storage, a 9,000-square-foot painting bay, and 12 acres of outdoor working area. Production capacity reaches 500 tons per month or 8,500 man-hours per month. Equipment includes CNC plasma cutting (11'6" x 50'), a CNC drill line (40" x 50'), a CNC angle clipper, a 300-ton press brake, plate rolling and shearing, structural sawing, and multiple overhead cranes up to 20 tons. The shop works with carbon steels (A36, A572, A709), stainless grades (304, 316, 316L), Inconel alloys, and high-nickel steel.

Universal Enterprises fabricates frac tanks, storage tanks, mud tanks, and skid tanks for the oil and gas sector, along with structural steel and plate work for construction and industrial customers. The company ships throughout the continental United States and internationally, with a regional service footprint covering numerous West Virginia counties.

The firm highlights its AISC certification and AWS D1.1/D1.5 welding qualifications, a shot-blast building with recovery system, and a climate-controlled paint facility as differentiators that support its quality commitments.

Customers include homeowners and businesses throughout Indiana seeking to reduce electricity costs and increase property value. The company markets its services directly to property owners and emphasizes a hassle-free process that includes a free 3D system model and in-person assessment.
